title: PMMSY IN CHHATTISGARH
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore from 2020-21 to 2026-27 (September, 2026) for the sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture in all the States and Union Territories including Chhattisgarh. The PMMSY scheme has significantly contributed to the development of the fisheries sector in Chhattisgarh by enhancing the financial, social, and economic security of fishermen and fish farmers through infrastructure, production, aquaculture expansion, technology infusion, support for welfare activities, market expansion and welfare interventions.
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India accorded approvals to projects under PMMSY worth Rs. 956.86 crore with a central share of Rs. 321.01 crore to Government of Chhattisgarh during last six years (2020-21 to 2025-26). Out of the approved central share, an amount of Rs. 274.16 crore was released to Government of Chhattisgarh in the last six years (2020-21 to 2025-26). In order to enhance the financial, social and economic security of fishermen , the major projects approved under PMMSY to the State are 28 numbers of Fish Seed Hatcheries, 3200 hectares of New Fish Ponds, 287 numbers of Re-circulatory Aquaculture System, 820 numbers Biofloc units, 14 nos. of Fish Feed Mills of various capacities, 511 numbers of Small Fish Transport Vehicles, 8500 Cages in Reservoirs and one Integrated Aqua Park (IAP) along with social security measures such as accidental insurance coverage of 5.52 lakh fishers annually, Livelihood and Nutritional support to 9667 fishers annually and improved access to institutional credit to 4189 fishers through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC). Collectively, these interventions have enhanced fish production (from 3.14 lakh metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 8.73 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25), increased farmers' incomes, promoted entrepreneurship, generated rural employment, reduced post-harvest losses, and contributed to the overall socio-economic development of the fisheries sector in Chhattisgarh.
This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) informed that under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), projects worth Rs. 956.86 crore (central share Rs. 321.01 crore) were approved for Chhattisgarh during 2020-21 to 2025-26, of which Rs. 274.16 crore was released. Key interventions include fish seed hatcheries, new fish ponds, biofloc units, cages, an Integrated Aqua Park, and welfare measures like insurance and Kisan Credit Cards for fishers. As a result, fish production in the state rose from 3.14 lakh metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 8.73 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25.
enrichment.context:
PMMSY is the Centre's flagship umbrella scheme for the fisheries sector, launched in 2020 with a total outlay of Rs. 20,050 crore initially (now stated as Rs. 20,750 crore up to 2026-27) under the Department of Fisheries. It aims to double fish production and exports, enhance value chain infrastructure, and improve livelihoods of fishers through a mix of central sector and centrally sponsored components, implemented alongside schemes like the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) and the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) extension to fishers. The scheme is part of the broader 'Blue Revolution' vision to make India a leader in fisheries and aquaculture, building on the earlier Blue Revolution Scheme.

Chhattisgarh, a landlocked state, exemplifies how inland fisheries and aquaculture (reservoirs, ponds, biofloc, cages) can be leveraged for livelihood diversification, especially for tribal and rural populations. The near-tripling of fish production in the state over a decade highlights the shift from traditional capture fisheries to technology-driven aquaculture (Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems, biofloc units, cage culture in reservoirs). Such data points are frequently used in Parliament to showcase scheme implementation and are relevant for tracking India's progress toward becoming a global aquaculture hub, a theme tied to food security, nutrition, and rural employment generation under GS Paper 3.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is implemented by which of the following?
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
prelims_questions.explanation: PMMSY is implemented by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, as stated in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an intervention under PMMSY in Chhattisgarh as per the given release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release lists fish seed hatcheries, new fish ponds, RAS, biofloc units, fish feed mills, transport vehicles, cages, and an Integrated Aqua Park, but does not mention deep sea fishing vessel subsidy for Chhattisgarh, a landlocked state.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in transforming inland fisheries in landlocked states of India. Use the example of Chhattisgarh to illustrate your answer.

mains_questions.question: Examine how technology-driven interventions such as biofloc units, recirculatory aquaculture systems, and cage culture can contribute to sustainable aquaculture and rural livelihood security in India.
